title: The Seventh Day and the Garden of Eden

verses.1: The heavens and the earth were finished, along with everything in them.
verses.2: By the seventh day God had completed His work, and He rested on the seventh day from all He had done.
verses.3: God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it He rested from all the work of creation He had done.
verses.4: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created. When the LORD God made the earth and the heavens,
verses.5: no shrub or plant had yet appeared on the earth, for the LORD God had not sent rain, and no one existed to cultivate the ground.
verses.6: Instead, water would rise from the earth and water the surface of the ground.
verses.7: The LORD God formed the man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
verses.8: The LORD God planted a garden in Eden, toward the east, and placed there the man He had formed.
verses.9: The LORD God made all kinds of trees grow from the ground — trees that were beautiful to look at and good for eating. The tree of life stood in the middle of the garden, along with the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
verses.10: A river flowed from Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided into four rivers.
verses.11: The first is named Pishon; it winds through the land of Havilah, where gold is found.
verses.12: The gold of that land is pure; bdellium and onyx are also found there.
verses.13: The second river is named Gihon; it winds through the land of Cush.
verses.14: The third river is named Hiddekel; it runs along the east side of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
verses.15: The LORD God took the man and settled him in the garden of Eden to tend and care for it.
verses.16: The LORD God instructed him: "You are free to eat from any tree in the garden.
verses.17: But you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for on the day you eat from it, you will certainly die."
verses.18: The LORD God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper alongside him."
verses.19: The LORD God had formed all the wild animals and birds from the ground, and He brought them to Adam to see what he would name them. Whatever Adam called each living creature became its name.
verses.20: Adam gave names to all the livestock, the birds, and the wild animals, but for Adam there was not found a helper alongside him.
verses.21: So the LORD God caused Adam to fall into a deep sleep. While he slept, He took one of his ribs and closed the opening with flesh.
verses.22: From the rib He had taken from the man, the LORD God formed a woman and presented her to him.
verses.23: Adam said, "At last — this is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She will be called Woman, because she was taken from Man."
verses.24: For this reason a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife, and the two become one flesh.
verses.25: The man and his wife were both naked and felt no shame.

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
